thread:
Sasha: alert from deploy-bot: missing audit rows for shard-3 14:00-14:40 UTC. Bringing eng-security here to triage.
Maya: saw 500s from audit-writer and an uptick in kms:request_errors around that window.
Liam: digging in. Migration changed roles.role_binding_id nullability and we merged a change that patched audit-writer to assume role_binding_id exists. Theres also a KMS signing error spiking. Two separate failure modes.
Liam: logs: 
```
2026-03-10T14:11:58Z audit-writer ERROR failed to sign event: kms:permission denied for key rbac-sign-key-v2
2026-03-10T14:13:02Z audit-writer INFO skipping event id=7823 because role_binding_id is NULL
```
Anika: I see an IAM deny for the roles service account to the key at 14:10. I re-applied the kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToSign binding for svc-account:roles@redwood. Should be propagating.
Sam: we need to treat missing audit rows as compliance-impacting. How many rows?
Maya: rough count ~1.2k events lost from shard-3 in that 40m window. Some were skipped, some failed on KMS. No customer-facing errors. Still P2.
DevOps Bot: deploy 1763051123 deployed rbac-schema-nullable-change to canary
Liam: immediate mitigation plan: (1) flip feature flag to disable schema-affecting writes (rbac-migration-lock) to prevent new NULL churn; (2) re-run backfill in small chunks with SKIP LOCKED; (3) replay audit events from kafka backups to an async ingestion queue that doesn't block on KMS signing.
Maya: agree. I'll flip rbac-migration-lock now (will route new binding writes to legacy codepath).
Maya: flipped flag. New role-binding writes are on legacy path.
Sam: can we avoid double-signing when we replay? Need idempotence.
Liam: replay tool supports dedupe by event_uuid. Use `--allow-duplicates=false`. For signing we have two options: (A) ensure KMS path works, or (B) replay unsigned into an internal queue marked for delayed-signing once KMS healthy. I'd prefer B for safety.
Anika: KMS: key status ENABLED, last-rotation 2026-01-18. I reattached IAM role to svc-account. Also raising a KMS guardrail ticket to alert on transient IAM changes.
Maya: backfill plan (canary first): chunk size 500, order by id, use FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, update computed role_binding_id via stable compute_binding function. Example command:
````
psql -c "BEGIN; WITH c AS (SELECT id FROM roles WHERE role_binding_id IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT 500 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED) UPDATE roles SET role_binding_id = compute_binding(id) FROM c WHERE roles.id = c.id; COMMIT;"
````
Liam: also validate compute_binding deterministic id->binding mapping. Add checksum compare against backup copy before commit.
Maya: running shard-1 canary now (will update).
Maya: canary done: 470 rows updated, no locks, no regressions. Audit-replay queued 320 events to audit-replay-queue (unsigned).
Liam: good. For shard-3 we should ensure replay reads from kafka topic `audit-events-raw` partitions 3-5 offsets 120000..120800 and push to `audit-replay-queue` with metadata event_uuid preserved. Use: `tools/replay.py --topic audit-events-raw --start-offset 120000 --end-offset 120800 --to-queue audit-replay-queue --allow-duplicates=false`
Anika: KMS metrics: denies gone after IAM rebind. No more permission_denied in the last 12m.
Sam: I'll open INCIDENT-2026-0457 public/private notes and ping Compliance: compliance@redwood.ai. Also create follow-ups: add unit tests around audit-writer short-circuits and integration test for KMS failover path.
Sasha: agreed. Action items recap:

- Liam: run kafka replay into audit-replay-queue, monitor audit-writer 5xxs and kms:request_errors.
- Anika: verify KMS bindings and create IAM guardrails ticket (KR: alert on cryptoKey IAM changes).
- Sam: incident notes + Compliance notif + unit/integration test tickets.

Liam: post-recon scripts: `python tools/rbac/recon_counts.py --start 2026-03-10T14:00 --end 2026-03-10T15:00 --compare roles_role_bindings, audit_log`
Maya: shard-3 canary finished: 1,030 rows updated. Audit-replay-queue accepted 890 events; worker is signing them once KMS is healthy.
